principles.rule: Use intention-revealing, pronounceable, searchable names. Names state why something exists and how it is used. No encodings, no noise words, no cute names.
checks: no single-letter names except tiny scopes

principles.rule: Keep functions small and do exactly one thing at a single level of abstraction.
checks: extract until each function does one thing

principles.rule: Minimize function arguments (0-2 ideal, avoid 3+). No boolean flag arguments; use argument objects when needed.
No side effects; apply Command-Query Separation. A function either does something or answers something, never both.
Eliminate duplication (DRY). Duplication is the primary enemy of maintainable code.
Express intent in code, not comments. Avoid redundant/commented-out code; delete dead code. Keep only legal, intent, warning, TODO, and API-doc comments.
Format for readability: related code close together, dependent functions near each other, short lines. Follow team conventions over personal style.
Respect the Law of Demeter; avoid train-wreck call chains. Objects hide data and expose behavior; data structures expose data and have no behavior.
Prefer exceptions to error codes. Do not return or pass null; use special-case objects or exceptions. Provide context with errors.
checks: no null returns from public APIs
error handling isolated in its own functions

principles.rule: Wrap third-party APIs behind your own interfaces/adapters; do not let external types leak through the system. Use learning tests for unfamiliar libraries.
checks: external library types not exposed in core APIs

principles.rule: Keep tests clean and treat them as first-class code. Tests are FIRST: Fast, Independent, Repeatable, Self-validating, Timely. One concept per test. Prefer TDD.
Keep classes small with a single responsibility and high cohesion. Organize for change (OCP/DIP) and isolation.
Follow Kent Beck's rules of simple design in order: (1) passes all tests, (2) no duplication, (3) expresses intent, (4) minimal classes/methods.
checks: design is the simplest that passes tests and expresses intent

principles.rule: Apply the Boy Scout Rule: always leave the code cleaner than you found it.
checks: opportunistic small cleanups in touched files
